summary: 3DNow! SIMD interpolation between four packed float control points (a2..a5) parameterized by scalar factor a6, storing two result lanes into output a1. Broadcasts a6, derives a set of higher-order weight coefficients with packed multiply/add/difference/sign-flip operations (including a packed sign flip via 0x8000000000000000 and a scale by packed [2.0f, 3.0f] 0x4000000040400000), blends the first packed element of all four inputs, blends the full second packed element of all four inputs, scales both results by packed 0.5f (0x3F0000003F000000), emits EMMS, and returns a1.

operations.description: Broadcast scalar factor a6 into packed 32-bit lanes via cvtsi32_si64 and punpckldq, constructing the t and 1.0f operands (v6, v7, v8); powers t^2 and t^3 are derived from these.

Derive weight coefficients from t: packed differences (v12), a scale by packed [2.0f, 3.0f] 0x4000000040400000 (v13), a sign flip via pxor with 0x8000000000000000, and lane shuffles (v14..v20) producing the coefficient lanes used to blend the control points.
Blend the first packed element of the four control points: v22 = w0*a2[0] + w1*a3[0] + w2*a4[0] + w3*a5[0] using packed pfmul/pfadd.
Blend the full second packed element of the four control points: v23 = w0*a2[1] + w1*a3[1] + w2*a4[1] + w3*a5[1] using packed pfmul/pfadd.
Scale the first blend by packed 0.5f (0x3F0000003F000000) and store the full 64-bit pair at a1[0].
Scale the second blend by packed 0.5f and store the full 64-bit pair at a1[1].

Reads four SIMD constant globals qword_5AF900, qword_5AF910, qword_5AF920 and qword_5AF968; in the decompiled source these appear folded into inline __m64 literals, so the per-global constant identity is not recoverable from the packet.
Emit 3DNow! EMMS (_m_femms) to clear the MMX/3DNow state before returning.

unresolved: Per-global mapping of qword_5AF900, qword_5AF910, qword_5AF920 and qword_5AF968 to the folded __m64 literals is unknown; the packet does not link each constant to its global.

The exact per-lane weight coefficient formula was not fully derived from the packed shuffle/sign-flip sequence; the canonical name implies a cubic Bezier shape but that intent is inferred from the instruction structure only.

Field base this at +0x8 records reads from the second packed element of all four input control points; the underlying input array layout is caller-defined and equal offsets on unrelated this pointers are not proof of a shared class.
Packet labels field base this +0x8 as read-only, but the raw source also writes a1[1]; the rw flag may reflect only a subset of the access sites.
